#3259. Black Friday Sales Are Days Away, but Most US Adults Aren’t Waiting, CNET Finds

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Over one-third have already started holiday shopping, but November's sales could yield big savings.

Even though early holiday sales started months ago, shopping your wish lists during Black Friday and Cyber Monday sales may be worth the wait if you’re one of the few planning to shop November sales. It’s the time to save money on most tech devices. But holiday shopping could look different for US adults juggling smaller budgets and shopping frustrations.

CNET’s annual holiday shopping survey shows that 27% of US adults plan to start holiday shopping in November and 17% plan to shop during sales. However, US adults will be juggling a smaller tech budget of $808. That’s $123 less than CNET’s survey findings last year.

Finding savings is paramount to staying within your price range this year, but how can you spot a good deal when nearly every retailer is having a sale? CNET experts weighed in on US adults’ holiday shopping plans and shared expert advice to score the best Black Friday and Cyber Monday deals on must-haves.

CNET found that 27% will plan or start their holiday shopping this month, with 17% of November shoppers planning to shop holiday sales, like Black Friday and Cyber Monday.

The big question is whether the sales are worthwhile. CNET’s director of commerce content, Russell Holly, says it comes down to when you find a deal on a must-have item.

“The best time to buy is the moment you see something you want on an actual discount, because increased prices can come at any time,” Holly said.

Holly says even steep discounts aren’t lowering prices as much as before, but the right deals may make you reconsider. You just have to know where and when to shop for tech devices.

For example, Black Friday is usually the best time to buy electronics, including TVs and robot vacuums, with the biggest deals lasting from Black Friday to Cyber Monday.

CNET’s senior laptops editor, Matt Elliott, says if you’re planning to buy a new laptop during holiday sales, look for discounts at Amazon, Best Buy and vendor sites like Dell, HP and Lenovo.

“These retailers and companies are constantly rotating discounts on laptops, and these sales can save you hundreds of dollars. So, it’s worth tracking the price of a laptop you want and buying it when it dips,” said Elliott.

Black Friday and Cyber Monday are also a good time to buy the latest wearables, said CNET’s wearable expert, Vanessa Hand Orellana.

“For Black Friday, all the heavy wearable hitters tend to go on sale: Google, Samsung, Oura, Garmin and Apple,” said Orellana. However, if you don’t need the latest tech, you can find some of the best deals on last year’s tech at third-party retailers, like Best Buy and Walmart. And many of the previous-gen models share the same features as the newest ones, said Orellana.

CNET’s deals team spends hours making sure sales are legitimate — not just a fake price drop. And in the coming weeks, they’ll track deals on devices like laptops, headphones, wearable devices and smart home gadgets, plus alternatives to more costly tech, to help you determine what’s worth buying now or later.

You can also check an item’s price history to see if you’re getting the best deal by using price trackers like CamelCamelCamel and comparing prices across retailers before buying. But as Holly noted, if you want to upgrade your personal devices, don’t wait. Look for the best price you can find and buy it right away. Otherwise, prices may go up while you wait.

Last year, CNET found that US adults planned to spend an average of $931 on holiday shopping. This year, shoppers are planning to spend less.

On average, they expect to spend $808 on holiday shopping. That’s $123 less than last year. Some generations plan to spend more, such as millennials, who anticipate an average holiday shopping outlay of $1,074. Boomers will spend around half that amount — $582.

Higher everyday living costs could explain why holiday budgets are lower.“Everything else being more expensive means less left over for gifts,” said Holly. “There’s very little indication that component prices are going to come back down anytime soon, so if you’re hoping for the kinds of prices you saw even two years ago, I would say you’re going to be waiting quite a while.”

Balancing holiday gifts and everyday basics on your usual income can be a lot to handle. Now’s the time to set holiday expectations, including a budget and a list of must-haves, along with more affordable options that still meet your needs.

Then keep checking prices and deals from your trusted retailers and be prepared to buy when you spot good savings. Most importantly, try to avoid using credit cards and buy-now, pay-later plans that can lead to debt. The Federal Reserve’s recent rate hike held rates elevated, which means borrowing costs will remain high and make debt more expensive through higher credit card and loan interest rates.

CNET found that 73% of shoppers plan to buy tech products or services this season, but what most US adults plan to buy and how much they plan to spend may surprise you.

Thirty percent of shoppers plan to purchase toys, and 25% plan to buy kitchen items, such as air fryers and cookware. But shoppers don’t plan to buy as many personal electronics and home entertainment products. Only 20% plan to buy headphones or earbuds, and even fewer plan to buy video games for consoles (18%) or laptops and TVs (11%). More shocking is that only 13% plan to buy phones. We’ve seen prices increase across popular tech devices and brands due to the RAM shortage, which has led to low supply and high demand for memory chips.

Some of the latest releases cost way more than the average $808 most US adults plan to spend. For instance, the $2,000 iPhone Duo alone costs even more than the average $1,704 that millennials plan to spend on tech this holiday season. And less costly phones are still beyond holiday budgets, like the $1,200 iPhone 18 Pro Max, and even the iPhone 18 Pro is $1,200. Trade-in offers and sales can help lower that cost if you’re planning to upgrade, but shop around and compare deals before buying.

Increased prices may make you reconsider whether to stick with your current model or upgrade, but remember, you have options.

“If the current laptop works well enough, upgrading can either be viewed as a luxury purchase for later or shifted to buying used or refurbished models to save extra,” Holly said.

You may also consider a slightly older model of the device you’re looking for. It could still have all of the features you need, but cost less. Another money-saving option is to consider refurbished tech that’s in excellent or good condition from a certified refurbished retailer. You may still notice some price increases due to demand, but it could still cost less than the newest models.

Most US shoppers (84%) expect the holiday shopping season to come with a few hurdles this year. Forty-three percent are concerned about deceptive pricing practices, such as retailers raising original prices before discounting them for a sale. Others are concerned about deals selling out immediately because of low stock or automated buying bots (39%).

But if you’re more worried about fake deals or sales being a money grab by retailers, Holly said that historically, there have been some great sales ahead of the holidays. It’s still best to do your research before buying to make sure you’re getting a deal by comparing retailer prices before and after announced sales and using price tracking tools, like CamelCamelCamel. Heads up that many retailers, like Amazon, have flash sales with specific times of deeper discounts, and you’ll need to act fast, so it’s best to plan your holiday shopping now.

“The best thing anyone can do ahead of a shopping event is prepare,” said Holly. “Find your favorite price tracker tool before the event starts, have a general idea of what you’re looking to buy and be sure to keep an eye out for bigger discounts when you bundle things together.”

CNET commissioned YouGov Plc to conduct the survey. All figures, unless otherwise stated, are from YouGov Plc. The total sample size was 2,615 adults, of whom 1,552 were interested in purchasing consumer tech products or services this winter holiday season. Fieldwork was undertaken Sept. 3-6, 2026. The survey was carried out online. The figures have been weighted and are representative of all US adults (aged 18 and older).

#3257. Google is making it easier to opt out of Gemini AI model training – here’s how

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

You’ll soon be able to turn off Gemini model training but still retain access to your previous chats with Google’s AI.

Also: I checked Gemini’s new Memory summary to see what it knew about me

In a change set to roll out in the coming weeks, you’ll be able to put the brakes on Gemini model training without losing access to your previous conversations with the AI. Here’s how this works now — and how it will work down the road.

Currently, Gemini offers a setting called Keep Activity that controls not only whether and for how long your chats are saved but also whether they’re used to train the AI. You can’t separate the two.

To correct this problem, Google will replace Keep Activity with two new settings. With the first setting, you’ll be able to keep or delete your past chats and choose how long your history will be saved. With the second setting, you’ll be able to decide whether your chats, including all text and attachments, will be used for model training.

Also: I asked Gemini Notebook to ‘make me a site’ from my notes

“With this change, you will be able to keep your history while independently controlling generative AI model training,” Google said in an announcement shared to Gemini users via email.

Here’s how this will play out. If your Keep Activity setting is off when this change is made, both new settings will be off. If your Keep Activity setting is on, both new settings will be on. That means you’ll need to head to Gemini’s Settings if you wish to opt out of model training but still be able to view and access your previous chats.

ChatGPT offers a setting called “Improve the model for everyone,” which is double-speak for model training. But this is easy enough to turn off. Microsoft Copilot provides settings for “Training on conversation activity” and “Training on voice conversations,” both of which you can disable to opt out of model training. Claude’s AI training option is turned off by default. But you can always control this by checking the setting for “Help improve our AI models.”

#3256. Is Lowe's a Buy After Its Latest Earnings Report?

Both its sales and profitability figures required closer scrutiny.

By Eric Volkman – Updated Nov 20, 2026 at 5:47AM EST

10 stocks we like better than Lowe's Companies ›

Lowe's Companies (LOW +3.15%) stock enjoyed a midweek bump thanks to the third-quarter results it posted Wednesday morning. It was a beat-and-raise quarter for the durable home improvement and hardware retailer, with a near-double-digit increase in total sales. And while there was a large asterisk next to that figure, other positive developments helped lift the stock, at least initially.

The post-earnings share price pop was encouraging, although it evaporated the following day. Here's my view on whether the shares can go higher, and meaningfully, before long.

The quarter saw Lowe's post $22.8 billion in net sales, up an uncharacteristically high 9% year over year. At first glance, there was a mismatch between that growth figure and the comparable sales increase of 1.8%. This is due to the company's purchase of a new asset, wholesale construction materials distributor Foundation Building Materials (FBM), announced in August 2025. The deal closed in October, which was too late for FBM's full third-quarter 2025 results to be consolidated into Lowe's. Since the 2026 quarter included a full three months of FBM's performance, the year-over-year comparison for Lowe's total net sales was skewed.

Regardless, the line item exceeded the consensus analyst estimate of $22.4 billion.

As for net income, there was also a note next to both the GAAP and non-GAAP (adjusted) flavors of that number. On a GAAP basis, profitability was $1.67 billion, or just under 4% higher year over year. Translated into a per-share, adjusted figure, the improvement was barely over 1% (at $3.10). On top of that, refunds from the Trump administration tariffs that were ruled illegal put roughly $250 million in Lowe's coffers and juiced both GAAP and adjusted earnings per share (EPS) by $0.34. So what we can call organic adjusted EPS fell by almost 10%, to $2.76. The average analyst estimate for raw adjusted EPS was $2.89, and clearly, many investors were willing to ignore that refund-adjusted number and consider the raw one to be a beat.

As management teams habitually do, Lowe's attributed its improvements to its current Total Home Strategy initiative, which was announced in 2020 and updated in late 2024. This is an attempt to be an all-encompassing, one-stop, omnichannel retailer for every customer, be it a person needing a tool for a small repair or a construction industry pro working on large-scale projects with a sizable budget. Total Home Strategy was a big factor in the FBM acquisition and an earlier asset purchase in 2025, the interior surface design, distribution, and installation specialist Artisan Design Group (ADG).

Although the top- and bottom-line results for Lowe's were somewhat inflated, the company was confident enough to raise key guidance items. It now expects total sales of $92.5 billion for all of 2026; that's higher, if not dramatically so, than its previous forecast of $92 billion. Comparable sales are now expected to rise by around 0.5% over the 2025 results. That provided investors some fuel for optimism, as the preceding estimate was that the key indicator would be flat.

Lowe's maintained its adjusted EPS projection of $12.25, and its guidance for capital expenditures (up to $2.5 billion).

I find it admirable that Lowe's has articulated and is executing a clear and sensible strategy for growth (even if its all-things-to-all-clients nature might prove overly ambitious). I also like the fact that it's growing, if slowly, its sales and "comps" despite lingering weakness in new housing construction in this country.

Would that make me a buyer of its stock? To me, the jury's still out on the current iteration of the Total Home Strategy, which, like all grand initiatives, needs time to take full effect. I'd prefer to see concrete evidence that it's really boosting Lowe's results before pulling the trigger on an investment -- especially given the unspectacular third-quarter organic growth rates (or declines). So basically, I'd adopt a wait-and-see stance on the retailer's stock.

#3253. Your Googlebook just got a Chrome update – 5 new features

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

The Chrome update includes more useful vertical tabs, easier screen sharing, and some handy keyboard shortcuts.

On Monday, Google rolled out an M157 update for the Chrome web browser on Googlebook OS, with a handful of new features and performance boosts to streamline your workflow and browsing experience.

While the first Googlebooks on the market have received mixed reviews, these features could help the laptops gain more useful features in Chrome that other browsers already offer.

Also: Googlebooks? The best laptop for Android users is something else

Here are the five new Chrome features on Googlebook OS to know about.

If you’ve ever had to share your screen on a video call, you know how irritating it can be to switch tabs without having to repeatedly start and stop sharing. This Chrome update adds a tab-sharing controls bar; when you share a browser tab in a video call, Chrome will display a persistent control bar at the top of the window so you can “Stop sharing” or “Share this tab instead” from any tab.

Also: 6 Chrome default settings I changed to instantly

When you hover over a collapsed vertical tab rail with your mouse or trackpad, it will expand, so you can read full tab titles, switch tabs, or manage groups. The rail will collapse again when you move the cursor away.

This auto-expand feature is enabled by default. If you want to turn it off or on, go to Settings > Appearance > Tab position > “Auto expand tabs on hover,” or right-click the vertical tab rail.

The Chrome update allows you to manually resize your vertical tab bar to view longer page titles when needed. The browser will remember your custom tab width, even after you open a new window or restart the browser. (You’ll just need to turn “Auto expand tabs on hover” off for it to work.)

The system’s “Save As” file picker is now enabled by default for menu save actions, such as “Save link as” and “Save image as,” so you can more easily rename files and select a destination folder. This includes Google Drive or external storage.

Also: Google Chrome running slow? 5 easy ways to speed it up fast

Outside of these new features, a few of Chrome M157’s performance fixes include the ability to press Ctrl+L to reveal and select web addresses; keeping your bookmarks bar visible in fullscreen mode and while screen sharing; better media controls while using Picture-in-Picture mode; and the ability to partially translate PDFs within your browser.

If you have Chrome set up to automatically download and install updates, you won’t have to lift a finger to take advantage of the new features and performance boosts.

But if you’ve disabled automatic updates, you can manually update by selecting the three-dot menu in the top-right corner of your Chrome window and navigating to Help > About Google Chrome > Relaunch.

Also: My week with new Googlebooks: The good, the bad, and the promising

If the Relaunch option is greyed out or nowhere to be found, you’re running on the latest version of Chrome. And if you were working on something before the update, don’t worry: Chrome will save your open tabs and reopen them automatically when you restart.

#3249. Robinhood Markets vs. SoFi Technologies: Which Financial Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?

Robinhood's revenue jumped 51.6% last year, but SoFi trades at a lower forward multiple, and that gap could matter more than either growth story.

By Sarah Sidlow – Updated Nov 20, 2026 at 5:48AM EST

10 stocks we like better than Robinhood Markets ›

As the digital finance landscape evolves, investors are weighing the growth potential of Robinhood Markets (HOOD -1.09%) and SoFi Technologies (SOFI -0.59%) to determine which firm offers a better path forward.

While Robinhood started by democratizing stock trading for retail investors, SoFi began as a student loan refinancer before becoming a diversified bank. Both companies now compete for the same tech-savvy consumers by offering everything from credit cards to crypto trading, creating a compelling comparison between two major fintech players.

In its latest annual report, filed for the 2025 fiscal year, Robinhood highlighted its shift toward institutional services through the acquisition of Bitstamp. It is increasingly a major player in financial stocks by expanding its support for Bitcoin (BTC -3.67%) and other digital assets. The firm also maintains a joint venture, Rothera, to offer futures and derivatives trading for its retail and institutional users.

Reliable recent quarterly figures for at least one of these companies aren't available, so this comparison uses each company's latest full fiscal year. For the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, Robinhood reported nearly $4.5 billion in revenue, which reflects a 51.6% increase over the previous year. The company achieved a net income of approximately $1.9 billion, benefiting from heightened trading activity and the expansion of its subscription services.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the company carries a debt-to-equity ratio of nearly 1.3x, which measures total debt relative to shareholder equity. The current ratio is approximately 1.3x, measuring a firm's ability to cover short-term debts with assets that can be converted to cash within a year. Robinhood also produced roughly $1.6 billion in free cash flow, which is the cash remaining after paying for operating costs and capital expenditures.

SoFi Technologies is a member-centric digital financial services company that offers a comprehensive suite of banking, lending, and investing products. The company operates as a national bank and serves approximately 17.1 million members across its platform. It also leverages its technology segment to provide infrastructure to other fintech firms and partnered with Mastercard (MA +1.49%) to support its expanding card services.

During the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, SoFi generated nearly $3.6 billion in revenue, representing a growth rate of approximately 35.1% compared to the prior year. The company recorded a net income of roughly $481.3 million, a significant swing from its historical performance as it continues to scale its digital banking operations. This improvement highlights progress in monetizing its member base across multiple product lines, including lending and financial services.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, SoFi carries a debt-to-equity ratio of approximately 0.2x, indicating how much debt the company uses relative to its shareholder equity. Its current ratio is roughly 0.2x, which measures the company's ability to meet short-term liabilities with short-term assets. During the same period, the company reported a negative free cash flow of nearly $4.0 billion, representing cash from operations minus capital expenditures.

Robinhood Markets carries risks of heavy reliance on transaction-based revenue, particularly payment for order flow, which could be impacted by changing regulatory standards. The company also navigates significant litigation risks related to historical trading volatility involving stocks like GameStop (GME +0.91%). Its expansion into international markets like the European Union brings complex operational and regulatory challenges that could affect future growth.

SoFi Technologies is exposed to risks associated with its concentration in personal loan products, which could face higher default rates during an economic downturn. As a bank holding company, it must also adhere to strict capital requirements that may limit its operational flexibility compared to non-bank rivals. The company faces intense competition from legacy institutions such as Wells Fargo (WFC +1.08%) and Citigroup (C -1.07%).

Trading at a lower multiple of future Forward P/E estimates, SoFi Technologies appears to be the more value-oriented option for investors today.

Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.

SoFi stock has severely underperformed Robinhood Markets over the last three years, returning about 106% to investors vs. Robinhood's blistering 754%. But despite those results, I'd choose SoFi heading into 2027. SoFi trades at a lower earnings multiple and a smaller market cap, offering a lower-priced entry for fintech investors. In its latest quarter, it reported record adjusted revenue, EBITDA, net income, members, and products used, and raised its full-year guidance. Free cash flow was still negative at -$3.12 billion, negative FCF isn't uncommon for fintechs in growth mode, as loans held for sale are often recorded as cash outflows. In Q3 2026, loan originations hit a record $16.9 billion.

SoFi's product offerings were already more diverse than Robinhood's, and it now may be poised to recapture another important market: cryptocurrency. SoFi returned to crypto trading last year, allowing members to buy, sell, and hold more than 40 cryptocurrencies. It's also introduced a stablecoin, on-chain transfers, and a tokenized deposit, meaning it may be able to tap into some of Robinhood's biggest growth drivers while offering investors a broader financial services portfolio and a lower stock valuation.

#3248. Goodbye, Gemini Gems: How to use Google’s new Skills – and share them

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Google is retiring Gemini Gems. Here's what to do to access the same tools as Skills.

Google is replacing Gemini Gems with Skills starting Nov. 17, 2026, and it’s carrying over features that let you share Skills and add files from Google products.

Google has announced that it’s turning Gems, a Gemini feature that lets you create customizable AI chatbots, into Skills, which let you create custom instructions for Gemini. Any Gems you have created will automatically convert, but you can transfer them manually if you want to start using them now.

To help with the transition, Google revealed that two Gems features are moving, too: the ability to share creations and to include Drive, Notebook, and Photos files as part of your Skill’s instructions.

While the Gemini Gems feature is technically going away, any Gems you’ve created aren’t.

If you access the Gems portion of Gemini (since the feature is on the way out, you now have to access this through Settings), you’ll see a message that says “Starting November 17, 2026, we’ll automatically begin migrating all of your Gems to Skills.” (The cutoff date for accessing your Gems will be Dec. 16, 2026. Workspace business, enterprise, and non-profit accounts will get cut off in March 2027, and Workspace education accounts will be cut off in June 2027.)

A Gemini Skill functions much the same as a Gem. You describe specific situations when Gemini should use the Skill automatically and tell Gemini what you want the Skill to do (it’s best to give specific examples of output). Google gives the example of a marketing team sharing a brand-voice skill that references their brand guidelines doc in Drive, or a team lead sharing an onboarding skill based on the team handbook.

The biggest difference is that Gems were standalone chats, while Skills are custom instructions that work in any conversation.

You can create as many Skills as you want, but only 100 can be active at a time.

To get users familiar with Skills, Google is bringing over two features from Gems.

First, you can now share any Skill with other users. When you share a Skill, you can choose whether the other person has permission to edit or view only. To share a Skill, go to the three-bar menu in the top left > Customize > Skills. You can view or change permissions from that screen.

Also: I checked Gemini’s new Memory summary to see what it knew about me – how to see and edit yours

When a Skill is added, Gemini can use it automatically, or you can @mention it in chat to trigger it. One small caveat, though: you can only share Skills through the Gemini web app at the moment, not the mobile app.

Additionally, when you’re creating a Gemini Skill, you can choose to include files of up to 100MB from other Google products like Drive, Photos, and Notebook, along with files from your local device. Gemini will reference these files every time the Skill runs and update in real time, Google says. These features existed with Gems; Google is just moving them to Skills to make the new feature more comparable.

#3246. Perpetual Futures Are Surging in Popularity, But They Are Also Facing Mounting Controversy. Here's What Crypto Investors Need to Know.

Perps are coming to the U.S., and not just for crypto.

By Alex Carchidi – Nov 20, 2026 at 5:50AM EST

10 stocks we like better than Robinhood Markets ›

Perpetual futures ("perps") are coming to the U.S., and they're already a polarizing topic thanks to their availability on international crypto venues going back years. Robinhood Markets (HOOD -1.09%) said in September that it plans to offer them to U.S. users in the coming months, with up to 10-fold leverage on Bitcoin (BTC -3.67%) and Ethereum (ETH -5.50%) perps. Coinbase Global (COIN +1.73%) won approval to list stock perps in the U.S. this month. Hyperliquid (HYPE -9.37%) made a name for itself by tailoring its decentralized exchange to the needs of crypto perps traders.

But perps are controversial for the very same reason that they're so lucrative for these platforms to offer: Most investors lose, and the venue makes money no matter what happens along the way. Here's what crypto investors need to know about perpetual futures and why they will be one of the most important battlegrounds for regulators and businesses alike during the next few years.

A perpetual future is a financial derivative contract that tracks an asset's price and never expires for as long as it's held. They're almost always traded using leverage, or borrowed funds, which enables an investor's deposited collateral to control a far larger position than they otherwise could. And therein lie many of the factors that make perpetuals controversial.

Using a fairly volatile asset like Bitcoin as an example, with $1,000 in collateral and 10-fold leverage selected, the trader controls a $10,000 Bitcoin position. Thus, a 1% move upward in Bitcoin's price yields a $100 gain for the trader. However, if Bitcoin were to fall by 10% from the starting price, the position would be zeroed out, as the loss would be equal to 100%. Aster (ASTER -3.46%), a decentralized perpetuals exchange that competes with Hyperliquid, allows up to 1,001-fold leverage on Bitcoin, so a 0.1% price move down leads to a 100% loss.

Exchanges usually liquidate (forcibly close) positions well before collateral hits zero. One consequence is that being right about an asset's future price is completely useless if a price dip between the present and that future leads to liquidation before the prediction plays out.

Funding payments are automated recurring payments that keep a perp contract's price near the underlying asset's market price; when the perp's price is above the underlying asset's price, buyers pay sellers the funding payment, and vice versa.

Hyperliquid's documents set a baseline of about 11.6% per year paid by buyers to sellers, but the actual funding rate changes with market sentiment. For that Bitcoin position worth $10,000, that's $1,160 a year in fees, more than the original stake, assuming the coin's price doesn't move. But most perpetuals positions aren't held for long enough for that to occur anyway.

Most individual investors lose money when they dabble in perpetuals. The natural users of perpetuals are hedge funds, market makers, and other groups that are sophisticated enough to implement complex, systematic trading strategies without falling victim to the typical pitfalls.

Per some of its regulatory filings in Europe, Robinhood rates crypto perps seven out of seven for risk. According to a study this year by researchers at Stanford and Columbia universities, retail investors on Hyperliquid's exchange lost $1.1 billion from March 2025 through June 2026 by using perpetuals, whereas professional market makers brought in $208 million.

Nonetheless, perpetuals are coming to the U.S. in a big way. The Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) approved a Bitcoin perp on May 29, and stock perps were approved on Nov. 3.

Some are fighting back. Two lawsuits in particular argue that perps are actually technically swaps, which would make them a separate derivative category with different rules if the courts agree.

CME Group (CME +1.57%) is suing to halt crypto perps, and another group backed by Citadel Securities is suing to stop stock perps, arguing that the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) should oversee them rather than the CFTC. In opposition are Coinbase and the prediction market Kalshi, which are backing the CFTC in court. If the court sides with the challengers, stock perps could land under SEC rules that limit retail access.

Even if they're fully legalized and available, most smart long-term investors should skip perps because they're simply far too risky for non-professionals.

Buying the businesses or cryptocurrencies that will benefit from perp’s proliferation, like Hyperliquid and Robinhood especially, is likely the most straightforward way to get some upside from their increasing popularity.

#3244. Microsoft says its new AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5 at 5% of the cost

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Microsoft announced two new AI models at Ignite 2026 that promise impressive performance for much lower cost. They could reshape its relationship with OpenAI and Anthropic for good.

At today’s Microsoft Ignite 2026 keynote, the company introduced two new frontier AI models built for what the company describes as “everyday” coding tasks. But there’s a bigger story: what these models might mean for Microsoft’s AI costs and its dependence on OpenAI.

Microsoft claims its MAI Code 2 model shows 96% of Claude Opus 5.5 performance at 5% of Opus 5.5’s price.

Also: Microsoft wants to put a dollar value on AI’s work – but can you trust the math?

Microsoft says MAI Code 2 offers comparable performance to GPT-6.1 Sol or Opus 5.5 at a fraction of the cost. Microsoft’s Code 2 Flash model is comparable to the lower-end GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5, also at considerably lower cost.

This doesn’t mean that those of us who pay for $100/month subscriptions will suddenly get the equivalent for five bucks. Instead, these are usage-based metrics based on API usage.

It’s also important to understand that the benchmarks are all Microsoft-provided. Performance numbers may well differ once the models undergo independent performance tests.

Throughout Satya Nadella’s keynote, Microsoft showed slides referencing a wide range of foundation models that are intended to work with Copilot and other Microsoft offerings. Microsoft famously has a multi-billion-dollar investment in OpenAI dating back to 2023, and has built many of its products and services around OpenAI intellectual property.

But now, Redmond is benchmarking its internally built models against Anthropic and OpenAI offerings, and also touting that it’s integrating these new models as optional choices for GitHub Copilot, Microsoft 365, and Fabric.

Also: 75% of developers I surveyed prefer Claude Code over Codex

One thing that Nadella made clear in today’s keynote is how central AI is becoming in everything Microsoft does. Nearly all of those AI operations previously involved the company paying some token fees back to the frontier model providers or customers doing the same thing.

But with high-performing models of its own, Microsoft may become substantially less dependent on outside model providers, especially for the incredible volume of fairly basic and routine AI requests that occur across the company’s vast product line.

If you think back over the history of agentic work models like ChatGPT Work and Claude Cowork, you may recall that they originated as agentic coding tools. As users adopted the coding harnesses in Claude Code and OpenAI Codex to off-label productivity applications, the AI companies noticed and packaged work-centric agentic tools that were more non-programmer-friendly.

Also: I let ChatGPT Work and Claude Cowork loose on my files – only one made me nervous

There’s a lot of similarity between a coding agent and a work agent, including understanding a complex environment, using tools to change things, and producing reliable results. Coding turns out to be a very good environment for developing and testing these capabilities, particularly because code output is highly measurable. Coding agents are effective training grounds for non-coding work agents.

This becomes really interesting in today’s announcement. Along with Code 2 and Code 2 Flash, Microsoft announced MAI Work Flash, which it describes as having been derived from Code 2 Flash. Work Flash can help generate formulas in Excel, work with documents and instructions in Word, track decisions and extract useful information from Teams, and more.

Think about the level of intelligence these tasks are demanding from the AI models. Not that much. As long as the models are good enough, they’ll be good enough.

If Microsoft can reduce its expenses and use reliable models at a much lower price, the company itself will be able to save quite a bit of money across its entire software economy, while at the same time maintaining a deeper level of vertical integration and, therefore, control.

Let’s run some hypothetical numbers. Let’s say a company is spending $0.01 per AI request, which, with these new models, can drop down to $0.001 per request.

Also: Want to try ChatGPT Wallet? Read OpenAI’s liability disclaimer very carefully first

A company with a daily inference cost of a million dollars (a company like Microsoft, for example) could drop that daily cost to about $100,000. Add that up across a year, and the change in models could save $325 million annually.

A million here, a million there. Pretty soon, you’re talking real money.

There’s no direct evidence that Microsoft is trying to produce replacement models for the frontier providers’ offerings. But it is an interesting and compelling story if we look at Microsoft developing its own engines for the software it sells.

Microsoft says the numbers it’s reporting at are using a 50% introductory discount. That’s why I measured against $0.001 per request instead of $0.0005 per request above.

Benchmark selection could be cherry-picking. The numbers are impressive. But as we all know, there are lies, damned lies, and benchmark results. I’m fairly sure Microsoft isn’t padding these numbers too much, because it benefits from the new models more than even its own customers, but still. It’s an open issue.

The company also described clearly that these new models are not designed to handle the most challenging agentic and research workloads. You’re probably not going to use them to solve a decades-old mathematics challenge. But you’re very likely to use them to reformat your PowerPoint.

Speaking of reformatting your PowerPoint, Microsoft also emphasized that these new models did unusually well on visualization assignments. That’s a very good fit for not only UI design challenges but also graphics and slide production.

#3241. Here's the Average Social Security Benefit at Age 62

Claiming Social Security at 62 is the earliest option, but the check you receive may look very different from what you expect.

By Kailey Hagen, CFP® – Nov 20, 2026 at 6:00AM EST

The average 62-year-old collected $1,424.40 per month as of December 2025, the most recent data available from the Social Security Administration (SSA). Age 62 is the earliest you can claim Social Security, but it comes with a significant trade-off in the size of your check.

If your full retirement age (FRA) is 67, claiming at 62 means a permanent 30% reduction in your monthly benefit. Full retirement age ranges from 66 to 67, depending on your birth year, and it's 67 for everyone born in 1960 or later.

The SSA calculates your benefit based on an average of your wages across your 35 highest-earning years. Those earlier wages are adjusted for inflation and run through the primary insurance amount (PIA) formula to find your baseline check. Then, if you claim at 62, the government applies an early claiming penalty of up to 30% to your PIA.

Social Security was designed to replace about 40% of your pre-retirement income. That share is well short of what most retirees need, so many rely on savings or other income sources to cover their costs.

Gender differences in work history also impact these averages. The average benefit for men at age 62 is $1,572.83, while women receive $1,285.50, a gap of about $287.33 per month according to the SSA data from December 2025.

Claiming at 62 provides immediate cash flow, making it a popular choice for many who have stopped working. However, the trade-off is a much smaller check than you'd receive if you waited until a later age.

The average benefit for 70-year-olds is $2,274.68, which is $850.28 per month higher than the age-62 average. That amounts to about $10,203.36 per year in additional income for those who wait for the higher payout.

You tend to receive roughly the same total over your lifetime regardless of when you claim, if you live an average lifespan. At age 65, men are expected to live about 18 more years, and women about 21 more years.

The 3.6% cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) that will take effect in 2027 adds about $51 per month to that age-62 average. These adjustments are designed to help your benefits keep pace with inflation, though they can vary widely from year to year.

Seeing the $1,424.40 average helps you benchmark your own planning, but your specific check will ultimately depend on your career earnings and when you choose to file.

Claiming at 62 could actually give you a larger lifetime benefit if you have a short life expectancy. Those with chronic health issues or a terminal illness might prefer to claim as soon as possible rather than taking the chance that they pass away before they're able to apply.

Claiming Social Security at 62 can also make sense if you are unable to work and don't have enough personal savings to cover your expenses on your own. Even if you wind up with a smaller lifetime benefit, that's preferable to going into debt.

Married individuals whose spouse significantly outearned them throughout their career are typically better off claiming early, too. This might enable their spouse to delay Social Security until they qualify for bigger benefits. Then, when the higher earner applies, the lower-earning spouse can switch to a spousal benefit if that's worth more than their own retirement benefit.

For more on how Social Security affects your retirement, see this guide.

#3239. Microsoft wants to put a dollar value on AI’s work – but can you trust the math?

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

With Agent 365 Business Analytics, Microsoft could reshape enterprise spending, but there's a critical difference between estimated value and money saved.

We all know AI can get expensive. But does that expense result in real business value? That’s the trillion-dollar question Microsoft aims to answer with today’s introduction of Agent 365 Business Analytics.

Also: Microsoft says its new AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5 at 5% of the cost

Earlier this year, Microsoft introduced Agent 365, its tool for tracking agents the way an HR department would normally track human employees. With Agent 365 Business Analytics, Microsoft is attempting to build an accounting system for AI labor. The system attempts to calculate the economic value of the work performed by agents compared with what the agents cost, and then provide a return on investment estimate.

If it works, this is some very cool stuff. Microsoft is trying to map labor-market economics onto AI usage data to create value estimates.

Also: Work IQ is Microsoft’s big bet on agent-first enterprise IT, and I have questions

To do so, it uses real labor-costing information, including data from the US Bureau of Labor Statistics, the O*NET database from the US Department of Labor, and its own LinkedIn Occupational Graph.

This data, along with data gathered from Agent 365, is aggregated into analysis intended to answer:

The goal is to provide a comprehensive picture of AI spend against value produced.

Software accounting is long established and straightforward. We measure subscription fees, cost per seat, compute costs, burden costs (like floor space and other infrastructure), and more. But AI work doesn’t fit that model, making it very hard to quantify value.

Instead, Agent 365 Business Analytics measures cost both relative to human labor and in terms of technological expense. For example, it might look at a task and determine how much human effort that task would normally take, and then price that effort based on prevailing common labor rates.

Then, it might factor in how much of the task was actually done by a human vs. how much was contributed by an AI, along with the estimated value of the AI’s contribution. Then it mixes in the actual AI processing cost (whether in subscriptions, tokens, on-premises infrastructure, and cloud support).

Also: These Claude Enterprise features let you track AI ROI – what’s new

What comes out is a hybrid labor estimate that combines human contribution, human-replacement savings, AI costs, and then potentially AI savings over human costs. It sounds positively Orwellian. But the bottom line is that companies really haven’t been able to understand the AI bottom line.

There’s a catch. All these numbers are estimates. In its blog post, Redmond specifically says, “Assisted hours are a directional estimate of work AI helped complete, not measured time saved or financial return.”

In other words, what Agent 365 Business Analytics estimates might not actually line up with real-world experience or expenses. It’s also possible that AI work might have been assigned because there was AI to do the work, not that the AI was saving company labor costs with every token processed.

In other words, Microsoft may be able to tell you the economic value of AI-assisted work, but it can’t demonstrate definitively that the company saved any real money.

Also: 5 reasons your company needs a chief AI officer in 2026

I find it particularly telling that this is from the company that makes PowerPoint. Because now, with Agent 365 Business Analytics, it’s entirely possible that you could produce economic dashboards that look really, really impressive, but are entirely irrelevant to real life.

That’s not to say the product is useless. But it does go to the idea that you will have to be quite disciplined in how you interpret the results and how much stock you put in them for decision-making. It is one source of possible truth, not the source of absolute truth.

Microsoft has been investing for decades to build out the core infrastructure of enterprise computing. AI isn’t any different when it comes to the company’s overall mission.

With Agent 365 and the company’s related offerings, Microsoft wants to help you:

This means the company doesn’t necessarily have to provide you with the AI model to help you run your enterprise. With integration with offerings from OpenAI, Anthropic, Salesforce, Google, Databricks, Snowflake, and others, the company doesn’t even have to provide the apps or SaaS capabilities.

But if it can get in there and manage your plumbing, help you control costs, and be the HR operation for your AI workforce, Microsoft could own a central piece of your business’s operations.

The company also released new ROI tracking tools for companies monitoring their AI spend.

AI-powered workspaces are tech companies’ latest focus, as the industry still struggles to perfect adoption. Microsoft has just put its offering into the ring.

During the keynote for the company’s Ignite conference on Tuesday, CEO Satya Nadella announced Copilot Workspaces, a collaborative, “multiplayer” surface for Copilot’s agentic capabilities.

Also: Microsoft says its new AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5 at 5% of the cost

The product, available in Frontier for now, is similar to OpenAI’s ChatGPT Space and several new Anthropic features, including Whiteboard and Sheets, which essentially merge the work tools you’re used to using with an agentic framework.

“As the evolution of Copilot Notebooks, it’s where people and agents build on each other’s work,” Microsoft said. “An agent drafts a section of a document, and you review. You leave a comment, and an agent picks it up.”

Microsoft also announced Autopilot, a sort of counterpoint agent to Copilot that “can watch Teams channels, follow up on emails, run recurring work, and manage a project — without waiting for a prompt,” as Microsoft described.

In a demo video during the keynote, the agent appeared to function similarly to OpenAI’s Dots, but for work — employees can tag their Autopilot “like a colleague,” Microsoft said, and assign it tasks.

Also: 4 ways Anthropic’s new Claude Sheets beat using a Google Sheets connector

Microsoft said the agent will be able to autonomously handle “meetings and follow-ups on its own,” though that claim may be best verified by teams themselves.

Speaking of trust, however, Microsoft noted that “Autopilot runs on the identity, security, and compliance foundation IT already uses,” and that “each Autopilot has its own Microsoft Entra Agent ID and a named manager,” meaning IT can block it as needed.

“Its sign-ins and actions are logged under its own name, so security teams have a clear audit trail. Powered by Work IQ, it understands how your organization works within existing permissions,” Microsoft said.

The company added that employees will soon “be able to bring their personal Autopilot into Workspaces” as well. The feature is also available in Frontier.

Nadella also announced a few other productivity features, including a “command center” called Today that spans email, calendar, meetings, tasks, and threads in Teams. Currently in private preview in Outlook and the Copilot app, it includes a personalized briefing and a feed of priorities that updates throughout the day.

“The draft is written and ready for you to edit; the schedule change is already proposed; and the forgotten follow-up is waiting for you to send it, complete with context so you can catch up quickly,” Microsoft said of the feature, which sounds like an agentic briefing-cum-morning-assistant.

Also: Nearly 70% of workers use AI regularly now – but many get no time to upskill

Microsoft also announced that Home, now generally available, unifies Chat and Cowork into a singular starting point. That’s similar to Anthropic’s recent consolidation of its chat and agentic Cowork offerings, demonstrating an overall trend toward simplification in workplace AI.

While more companies are finally starting to see a return on their AI investment, agents are still expensive and can quickly rack up costs when unsupervised.

Microsoft announced a few tools to track this at Ignite: Agent 365 Business Analytics and Agent 365 Cost Management.

Also: Microsoft wants to put a dollar value on AI’s work – but can you trust the math?

Agent 365, which Microsoft announced last year, is the company’s observability platform. Microsoft said Business Analytics, in Frontier Public today, provides insights on what a company is spending on AI and why, and where it’s paying off, as well as forecasts future costs. In a demo during the keynote, Microsoft showed how admins can see when specific agents’ costs have spiked recently and what (human) employee to notify as a result.

“It starts with a new way to measure your investment: in work completed, not simply tokens,” Microsoft said. “It analyzes the tasks, how long that work typically takes a person, and the share Cowork performed, providing a sophisticated view of the hours your intelligence supports and what the work is worth.”

Cost Management lets IT see where teams are using AI down to the model.

“Leaders can set spending policies, limits, and proactive alerts and control which models are available,” Microsoft said. Anthropic released a similar tool last month, though it was focused more on making seats as efficient as possible on Teams and Enterprise plans.

#3235. Windows’ Baseline Protection Can Simplify Security, but There Could Be Pitfalls

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

It makes security a little easier to manage, but apps can also refuse to work if your machine fails security checks.

Microsoft’s collecting all of Windows 11’s hardware-related security features under one roof starting in 2027. Announced during its Ignite developer conference this week, in addition to seven new AI models, baseline protection is a way to make Windows more secure out of the box.

The combination of core security safeguards into a single pass-or-fail device status is a boon, but it may also introduce problems, including for gamers, who tend to tweak aspects of the operating system environment, like UEFI BIOS settings.

A Microsoft spokesperson told CNET in an email that baseline protection is still in the preview stage and that the company will “continue to iterate and build upon this based on the feedback the company hears from customers, partners and developers.”

Currently, Windows’ eight key hardware security features are spread across the OS: the Trusted Platform Module security processor, Memory Integrity (which prevents unwanted alternation of data in memory), Kernel debugger protection (to guard the core code of the OS), Secure Boot (which ensures no tampering during system startup), driver security and a few others.

To manage or check these settings, you have to visit multiple locations, and if app developers need to verify them at runtime, they have to perform similar gymnastics.

The upcoming functionality will consolidate all those settings into a single control panel within Windows’ Security settings section, where you’ll be able to check their status and apply any necessary updates. Since it tracks all eight security features, developers will only need to confirm that baseline protection is met.

The feature is currently available in Windows Insider builds and is expected to roll out to the general public in 2027.

Baseline protection provides instructions for enabling these features if they’re not readily available. For example, enabling Secure Boot requires restarting directly into your BIOS. To save you time, the panel provides step-by-step instructions right on the screen, so you don’t have to look up how to do it yourself.

Application developers may have the biggest win here. The ability to poll just one security feature instead of eight individual ones streamlines the development process and allows developers to check security features quickly and easily. For instance, game anti-cheat software relies on multiple security measures to verify that no third-party code is running.

Microsoft has 11 initial software partners, including heavy hitters like Adobe, 1Password, Blizzard and Epic Games, each of which is incorporating support to help it identify risk faster, including detecting counterfeit and malicious software.

“A consistent security signal gives apps and organizations a shared foundation to build on,” said Michael Draper, vice president of Global Consumer Trust at Adobe, in a testimonial.

Power users and gamers potentially stand to lose the most from this new feature. Many of them intentionally disable certain security settings to dual-boot Linux, run custom hardware drivers or improve gaming performance by disabling Virtualization-Based Security, which can lower frame rates and cause visual glitches.

Also, since developers can perform a single pass-fail check for all the settings, users may be shoehorned into keeping all eight features enabled, even if the developer doesn’t need them all.

Microsoft is leaving enforcement up to the developer, though. For example, an application may check baseline protection, see that it’s not fully satisfied, but allow a user to run it anyway with a warning screen or another pop-up or reminder. Alternatively, the software may refuse to run until the user enables full baseline protection.

“Windows baseline protection gives the app information on each security requirement, and developers can choose to enable some or all requirements,” said a Microsoft spokesperson. “Microsoft still recommends developers embrace all requirements to meet the strongest security bar.”

Adobe, Blizzard, 1Password and most of Microsoft’s other partners haven’t expressly said they’ll lock users out of apps without complaints, but a few have strongly hinted that this will be the case.

Grand Theft Auto VI offers a size befitting the 13-year wait. Not only is the Vice City map absolutely huge, but it’s the most system-rich and mechanically deep game in the Grand Theft Auto series to date. There’s an overwhelming amount of things to see, do, and learn.

Like millions of gamers worldwide, I dived into the game at midnight, the very second it unlocked on my PS5 Pro. I’ve since put five hours of playtime into GTA 6, and while I’m still getting my head around all that the game has to offer (my completion percentage is a mere 12%), I’ve already learnt a few lessons the hard way. Yes, mistakes have been made.

So, if you’re heading to Leonida over the weekend, here are three major mistakes I've already made, and most importantly, how you can avoid doing the same stupid things as me (all spoiler-free). Learn from my errors!

After 13 years of waiting, Grand Theft Auto VI has arrived. Set in the state of Leonida, with Vice City at its heart, you play Jason and Lucia, two criminals forced into an increasingly dangerous situation as they seek their fortune, discovering the darker side of the sunniest spot in America.

GTA 6 introduces a new money system in which you can hold cash either on your person or stashed securely at your safehouse. If you get “wasted” or “busted” by the cops, you’ll lose all the money you’re carrying, but the funds kept under the floorboards at Jason's beachside home are protected.

As a cautious type, I took this to mean never carry any money on your person for fear of losing it, which pretty quickly proved to be an oversteer when an early mission required me to buy a gun, and I literally had $0 in my wallet. This forced a trip back to the safehouse, where I counted out the exact number of bills required to buy the weapon.

Once I returned to the Ammu-nation store, I bought my gun and then was presented with a range of attachments (some with a limited-time discount), which I couldn’t buy because, again, I’d only brought the specific amount required to buy the gun itself. Frustrating.

This taught me not to fear actually carrying money in your wallet. Sure, running about Vice City with your entire bank balance on hand is probably unwise, but you’re going to want, and need, some money in your pocket. At this early stage, I’ve been opting for a 50/50 split, keeping half my ill-gotten gains in my stash, and the other half within instant reach.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

My approach to previous GTA games tended to be this: Complete a few story missions, and then go on a psychotic rampage to blow off some steam (I swear I’m not a total psycho).

GTA 6 is different. For pretty much the first time in the franchise’s history, the game actively discourages you from causing carnage without purpose through the new “Criminal Profile” system. Your in-game actions are tracked and contribute to the type of criminal Jason (and later Lucia) is becoming. Ranging from a “professional” all the way to a full-blown “psycho.”

During my first GTA 6 session, after completing the mandatory prologue, I decided to see how many wanted stars I could rack up with just the starter pistol, and pretty quickly the game warned me that my criminal spree would have consequences. It felt like that old Tellale’s The Walking Dead warning message, “Clementine will remember that…”

Rockstar has confirmed your “Criminal Profile” will impact how the story plays out, and I certainly don’t want to receive a “bad” ending; such was my concern about how my early game rampage would impact how my GTA 6 story plays out, I opted to reload to a previous save to instantly wash away the worrying amount of blood already on Jason’s hands.

So, in GTA 6, it pays to show restraint. You will commit many crimes, of course, but resist the urge to go full GTA and instead commit your criminal acts with purpose and even planning.

Speaking of planning, from what I’ve played so far, GTA 6 is the most ambitious Grand Theft Auto yet in all areas, including mission design. Previous GTA games present players with cinematic but largely linear missions; if you tried to get creative, the game would quickly shepherd you back onto the golden path with instant fail states for any deviations.

To be clear, GTA 6 does have these types of missions as well, but there’s a larger focus on player choice and letting you pick your approach. As an early (spoiler-free) example, a Chapter 1 mission asks you to retrieve a red sports car from a police impound lot.

You’re dropped off right outside the main gate, with an on-screen prompt encouraging you to break the lock. Naturally, I obliged, and the impound’s alarms started blaring; every cop in the area was instantly alerted, and the mission pretty much went further south from there.

One reload later, I was back at the mission start, and this time, I slowed down. I cased the joint first, walking the perimeter, trying to find a subtler way to access the impound lot. And what do you know, a conveniently placed scissor lift around the corner got me onto the roof, allowing me to quietly drop into the compound without setting off any alarms or alert cops.

It’s a reminder that in GTA 6, thinking before you act can pay off, and when you factor in the “Criminal Profile” system, there is real merit in completing missions without having to shoot your way out of trouble.

#3231. Microsoft’s new Licensed Weights lets businesses customize AI models with their own data

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Microsoft is bridging the gap between proprietary and open-weight AI while targeting data-conscious businesses.

During the keynote at its Ignite conference on Tuesday, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella announced several new models from Microsoft AI (MAI), its lab within the company. But new model releases are almost a dime a dozen these days, and accelerating fast — what really stood out was how Microsoft will let its customers access those models.

Also: Microsoft says its new AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5

MAI said it would allow its customers to customize its frontier models with their own data and run them securely in Azure through an initiative called Licensed Weights. It’s essentially a selective approach to open-weight AI: more so than proprietary models from OpenAI and Anthropic, but not fully downloadable on Hugging Face like Mistral’s Le Chonk. Interested companies will need to go through their Microsoft account reps to get started.

“You control who can access it. Your data and adaptations stay entirely yours. And we’ll work with you through Frontier Company to deliver the custom model and embed it in your own products and agents,” Mustafa Suleyman, CEO of MAI, said during the keynote.

The approach should stand out to businesses looking for affordable AI that lets them retain control over their IP. Microsoft said it would only use customers’ information to train its models if they agreed.

“No one wants to pour their IQ into someone else’s model,” Suleyman said during the keynote, a nod to an argument Palantir CEO Alex Karp has made repeatedly.

The dominant, if simplified, narrative in AI has been that proprietary, expensive models boast peak capabilities but aren’t customizable, while open, cheaper models are customizable but less capable. Microsoft’s AI models don’t necessarily compete with OpenAI and Anthropic yet, but the company has legacy sway with countless businesses. By offering a customizable AI option, it could strike a balance among major tech companies.

Western labs, including Thinking Machines and Mistral, are releasing more competitive open-weight models, but Anthropic and OpenAI still have the overwhelming majority of the enterprise AI market. Though Licensed Weights isn’t an open-weight family of models, it does diversify the open-versus-closed debate a bit and differentiate Microsoft’s offering from OpenAI’s and Anthropic’s. It’s also a smart pairing with Microsoft’s goal to balance price and performance, if businesses find it impressive enough.

Also: Microsoft unveiled Copilot Workspaces at Ignite 2026

“Averaged over four widely used benchmarks that target the everyday enterprise coding tasks we see in GitHub Copilot, MAI Code 2 gives you 98% of the performance of GPT 6.1 Sol at just 40% of the cost, and against Opus 5.5 it’s an incredible 5% of that cost,” Suleyman said of the new coding model the company announced at Ignite.

The company also released its new image editing model, MAI Image 2.7, on Tuesday, which now leads the category on Artificial Analysis while beating Nano Banana Pro and several GPT image models on price and quality. With Licensed Weights, Microsoft has positioned itself for organizations seeking a reliable blend of ROI tools, customization, security controls, and capability.

If you’ve ever bought a new TV and invited a tech nerd like me into your living room, you already know I’m grabbing your remote, diving into the picture settings, and disabling motion smoothing.

For movies and prestige TV, it is a crime against humanity — turning a cinematic masterpiece into an episode of "Days of Our Lives" shot on a camcorder. I hate it. Tom Cruise hates it. You should hate it too.

And yet, here I am, playing Grand Theft Auto VI with motion smoothing cranked on, and refusing to turn it off.

To understand how I ended up committing TV heresy, you have to understand the shock to the system that is GTA 6’s frame rate. Coming straight from my monster PC rig playing games like Resident Evil Requiem at up to 214 FPS, dropping back down to a strict 30 FPS console lock feels like wading through treacle.

But on top of that, as I’ve seen (and you’ve seen on Digital Foundry’s test), that 30 FPS lock isn’t an actual lock. It can dip into the mid-20s during heavy scenes. Coming from super fluidity, that 30 FPS is brutal to adapt to.

So out of sheer desperation (and because we’re stuck waiting for the PC port), I broke the golden rule and toggled my TV’s smooth motion setting on.

And I hate to admit it, but it’s basically bootleg DLSS Frame Generation for your living room.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Just like PC frame generation tricks of old, your TV’s motion interpolation processor looks at two real frames from your console, guesses what should happen in between them, and inserts an artificial frame to smooth out the motion.

The moment I flipped it on in GTA 6, that nauseating camera stutter when cruising down Ocean Beach vanished. Panning around a crowded street or taking a high-speed corner suddenly felt dramatically more fluid — nowhere near 60 fps, and definitely not my desktop rig, but miles smoother than the choppy presentation.

Before the AV forums come for my head with pitchforks, let’s be completely honest about the trade-offs. There is no such thing as a free lunch in frame interpolation:

Because your TV has to wait for the next frame before it can invent the one in the middle, motion smooth adds latency between pressing a button and seeing the result on screen. In twitchy, competitive games, that’s a death sentence.

But in a Rockstar open-world game — where character movement is already famously weighty and deliberate — I never noticed that extra latency.

Your TV’s processor is just guessing after all, and while it is a good guesser, there are some moments of weird shimmering around fast-moving objects and some boiling around on-screen elements like subtitles. Probably compounded by the fact GTA 6 is already running its own resolution scaling tech under the hood.

Standard Game Mode and VRR (Variable Refresh Rate) automatically lock out motion smoothing on many TVs. Depending on your set, you either have to turn on the dedicated low-latency Game Motion Plus mode (found on newer Samsung and LG sets) or sacrifice VRR to unlock it.

The silver lining, though, is that with this being a 30 FPS game, it’s not high enough to require VRR anyway.

If GTA 6’s 30 FPS cap is giving your eyes a workout and you want to test the dark arts yourself, don’t just blindly max out every slider.

If your TV has a low-latency interpolation option (like Samsung’s Game Motion Plus or LG’s TruMotion tweaks), use that before turning off Game Mode completely.

Set Judder Reduction to a middle ground (around 5-7 out of 10) rather than maxing it out. You want to take the harsh edge off camera pans without turning your car into a blurry smudge.

This is optional based on personal taste. Test how your TV’s smoothing looks with GTA’s built-in motion blur turned off. For a lot of OLED owners, letting the TV handle the smoothing cleanly beats stacking two different blur effects on top of each other.

Do I want to play GTA 6 at native 240 FPS on my PC rig? Obviously. The second Rockstar drops the PC version, I’ll be uninstalling this hack from my brain and never looking back.

I still wouldn’t be caught dead watching a movie with motion smoothing turned on. But until PC gamers get their turn in Vice City, breaking the ultimate TV rule is the best survival trick I’ve found for making a 30 FPS masterpiece actually feel better to play.

Also yes, my wife has taken note of the fact that I share the same name as the male protagonist. And yes, she is side-eyeing how I treat Lucia hard.

A new AI model seems to drop almost every couple of days from one of the big tech giants, each improving on the previous version in one way or another. However, OpenAI’s latest and greatest are getting some pushback from developers and early testers. For the everyday user, the 6.2 Sol and Astra should perform more than serviceably, but those looking to dig in, test and use the new models for more professional work may run into some hiccups they’re not used to, according to some feedback.

Ethan Mollick, associate professor and director of the Generative AI Lab at the University of Pennsylvania’s Wharton School of Business, said in a LinkedIn post that GPT-6.2 Astra was “harder to steer and work with,” and “frequently seemed ‘lazy’,” compared with competitor models. Another brutal assessment on LinkedIn came from Jason J. Fleagle, head of AI at NETSYNC: “I think GPT-6.2 has to be one of the worst AI models OpenAI has ever released.”

However, there might be more to the story than that. OpenAI Codex leader Thibault Sottiaux, known as Tibo, mentioned in an X post that early builds of 6.2 Sol and Astra were released to influencers some time ago, that updates and changes were made to the models within the past couple of days, and that he assumes no retesting was done since. Only time and more testing will show whether these improvements make much of a meaningful difference.

OpenAI didn’t immediately reply to a request for comment.

#3228. Why Firefly Aerospace Stock Dropped This Week

There's more than one reason this space stock is falling to Earth.

By Scott Levine – Nov 20, 2026 at 6:03AM EST

10 stocks we like better than Firefly Aerospace ›

An analyst downgrade and market skepticism over a major engine contract sent Firefly Aerospace (FLY -1.05%) sliding 22.6% this week.

Firefly Aerospace stock changed hands at $19.52 as of the close on Thursday, Nov. 19, down 22.6% from Friday, Nov. 13's close through Thursday, Nov. 19's close, according to data provided by S&P Global Market Intelligence. Over the same period, the S&P 500 (^GSPC +0.00%) dropped 5.1%, and the Nasdaq-100 was down 5.1%.

The primary driver behind the decline was market scrutiny of Firefly's recent contract structure alongside a Wall Street Zen downgrade from hold to sell. Securities filings disclosed that AST SpaceMobile (ASTS +0.23%) issued 10 million shares to Firefly as part of an intellectual property license and rocket engine supply agreement valued at over $1.3 billion. Investors grew uneasy that a substantial portion of the contract relies on customer stock rather than guaranteed cash, while management also pushed back its Alpha Flight 8 rocket launch to early 2027. The sell-off leaves the stock down 68.6% (as of the close on Thursday, Nov. 19) from its 52-week high of $62.17.

Firefly Aerospace builds small- to medium-payload launch rockets, lunar landers, and orbital spacecraft for defense agencies, satellite operators, and commercial customers. In its last reported quarter ending Sept. 30, 2026, the company generated $110.7 million in revenue, up 259.6% year over year, while posting a net loss of $94.2 million. High production costs for its rocket line continue to weigh on profitability, keeping operational execution front and center for shareholders.

Firefly held $534.7 million in cash and short-term investments as of Sept. 30, 2026, providing liquidity to fund facility upgrades. However, taking customer stock to fund engine production exposes the business to secondary market volatility rather than securing immediate balance-sheet cash. Receiving stock instead of cash for its rocket engines shifts the AST deal from a liquidity boost to a bet on another speculative satellite maker.

With trailing price-to-sales (P/S) sitting at 9.4 against a $3.5 billion market capitalization, Firefly carries a valuation that demands steady operational progress. Investors will want to watch the initial flight tests for its Block II engine upgrade, currently scheduled for the first quarter of 2027, as well as the company's next scheduled earnings report on March 18, 2027.

Investors may have soured on Firefly stock this week after a downgrade from Wall Street Zen. Still, it's important to remember that this is solely one firm's opinion -- not an overwhelming consensus among a multitude of analysts. Therefore, investors should take it with a grain of salt.

Secondly, the delay of the Alpha Flight 8 launch until the first quarter of 2027 may also have disappointed investors. However, it stems from a national security customer's request rather than a company misstep.

While Firefly receiving AST stock instead of cash for engine licensing is a valid concern, it should hardly be enough to disqualify Firefly stock as a potential opportunity for exposure to the burgeoning space economy. Rather, investors should continue to monitor the company’s earnings reports carefully to confirm that Firefly continues to grow revenue and narrow its net losses.

#3227. I’ve tested Ubuntu 27.04 ahead of its April release – and it will wow you

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Tech > Services & Software > Operating Systems > Linux

I've been using Ubuntu 27.04, and the speed boost is noticeable. Here's what else is coming.

Ubuntu 27.04, Tenacious T-Rex, is set for an April 22, 2027 release. Although that seems a long way off, it’s sooner than you think. As is implied by the release number, 27.04 is not an LTS release, so it only receives support for nine months (until January 2028). The good news is that you can migrate from 27.04 to 27.10, and then to the LTS release, 28.04. The entire upgrade path ensures that you don’t have to miss a single release.

But what’s coming in Ubuntu 27.04? Given that it’s an interim release, you’re probably assuming that there’ll be nothing exciting to be found. Although there won’t be any game-changing additions, there will be plenty of refinements and bug fixes.

Also: I’ve used Ubuntu for 22 years – and 26.10 might be its best release yet

I’ve been using the daily release of Ubuntu 27.04 for a bit. Let’s take a look at what is currently expected in Tenacious T-Rex.

This is probably the biggest addition to the next release of Ubuntu. And although you won’t find any major changes in GNOME, there are some important ones. First off, there will be editable quick settings, which allow for customizing, adding, removing, and rearranging toggles and widgets. GNOME 52 will also enjoy a revamped calendar popover, which streamlines the feature to focus primarily on events, time, and weather.

Also: Over Ubuntu? Fedora is the Linux distro I’d hop to next – here’s why

There will also be several improvements to window management, such as a spatial overview and a mosaic/tiling system for auto-resizing and organizing windows, a refined full-screen Alt+Tab app switcher, which will be capable of grouping older windows by application while showing newer ones individually, and finally, the ability to remember window sizing, placement, and workspace.

Desktop search is also getting a bit of polish by way of a redesigned popover and an improved results overlay that includes file previews, multiple actions, and search filters. And, as usual, there will be plenty of bug fixes and performance enhancements. The bump in speed is noticeable, too, in my testing.

Ubuntu 27.04 will ship with the Linux 7.6 kernel, which includes better VRAM management for gaming and expanded support for modern hardware, such as early enablement for AMD Zen 6, stable support for Intel Xe3P, mainline boot capabilities for Apple M3 Pro/Max/Ultra, and initial support for the 2026 Steam Controller.

There will also be performance gains for both the Btrfs and Ext4 file systems, which (along with the improvements in GNOME 52) will make Ubuntu 27.04 one of the best-performing releases in some time.

Also: This lightweight Linux distro revives old PCs destined for the junk pile – and it’s beautiful

One thing that surprised me is that Myna (Ubuntu’s AI dictation tool) has yet to find its way into the Ubuntu ISO as a default app. As with Ubuntu 26.10, you can install it, but you have to first add the necessary repository with:

With the repository added, you can install it with:

Once installed, you can use it as expected.

As of right now, that’s all we know about Tenacious T-Rex.

It’s so early in the release cycle that it still uses the default 26.10 wallpaper, but there will be more information soon. I will say this: I’ve come to count on Ubuntu’s latest releases to be an improvement over the previous iterations, and from what I’ve seen so far in my testing, 27.04 will not disappoint. It may not knock you back to prehistoric times, but Tenacious T-Rex will wow you with its performance and polished looks.

The best Black Friday phone deals can save you hundreds of dollars on a brand new handset, but they're not the only deals available right now. There are plenty of phone accessories that are being discounted too, but choosing between them can be quite tricky.
